\begin{proposition}[The exact rooted elliptic-tree criterion and compact occurrence]\hypertarget{tag-01E7}{}\label{cdp:st:C.2.UN.61}
\StatementRecord{cdp:st:C.2.UN.61}{proved}{01E7}{\SeriesRef{cdp:st:C.2.UN.60}, \SeriesRef{cdp:st:C.2.UN.5}, \SeriesRef{cdp:st:C.2.UN.54}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.PT.3}, \SeriesRef{cdp:st:C.2.UN.28}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.PT.5}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.PT.6}, \SeriesRef{cdp:st:C.2.UN.31}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.PT.7}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.PT.8}, \SeriesRef{cdp:st:C.2.UN.58}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.PT.9}, \SeriesRef{cdp:st:C.2.UN.50}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.PT.11}; \cref{lem:II:zero-chern-elliptic-torsor}}

Let $S$ be a specified compact connected reduced SNC surface whose
incidence graph is a nontrivial tree. Distinguish one smooth component
$P$, with no initial restriction on its geometric genus or surface
type. Every other component is either a primary or secondary Hopf
surface, or is equipped with a specified fixed-Jacobian elliptic
quasi-bundle over $\PP^1$, with identity integral monodromy,
connected fibres and only smooth multiple fibre supports.
In the latter case every boundary curve is a fibre support of
the specified map. Retain the actual elliptic gluing maps
and the complete analytic torsors. The following finite
geometric test is necessary and sufficient for $S$ to occur
as a full fibre of a smooth-total degeneration of connected complex
two-tori.

\begin{enumerate}
\item The actual normal lines at every double curve are dual.
\item The root $P$ has a fixed-Jacobian elliptic quasi-bundle
$q_P:P\to B$ over a smooth elliptic curve, with identity integral
monodromy and only smooth multiple supports. Its marked boundary
curves are fibre supports, and every multiple fibre is marked.
Every other component is either a nonlinear algebraic-dimension-zero
Hopf leaf or an elliptic quasi-bundle over $\PP^1$ of the stated
type, whose multiple fibres are all marked double curves.
\item For each edge $e$, let $m_e$ be the exact finite order of
its normal line. It is the full elliptic multiplicity at each
elliptic endpoint and the resonance at a nonlinear endpoint.
Define the heights by \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.1}, with $V_0=\{P\}$.
There is an integer $R>0$ such that every nonlinear leaf has
$h_v=R$ and every elliptic nonroot vertex has $h_v<R$.
In the absence of nonlinear leaves any $R>\max_vh_v$ passes.
\item Perform the exact leaf-pruning operations of \ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.60},
retaining the complete inverse logarithmic charts, primitive fibre
directions, secondary integers and torsor transitions. The final
surface is a principal elliptic torsor $T_0\to B$. Its integral
Chern vector in $H^2(B,\Lambda_F)$ is zero.
\end{enumerate}

The normal-root maps identify the one fixed Jacobian $F$ along
the tree. The last condition refers to the actual analytic
inverse torsor; it does not replace it by its rational Chern
data. The pruning result is independent, up to the actual
marked isomorphisms of \ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.60}, of the order of disjoint operations.

Every support passing the test has a realization over $\PP^1$
with smooth compact total threefold. Its only singular fibre
is the given reduced $S$; every other fibre is a smooth
two-torus. All reduced fibre supports have Euler number zero.
Every component and every specified elliptic gluing map is
retained, including the complete torsor of every original
properly elliptic nonroot component.

In every actual occurrence the root is minimal,
$h^q(P,\OO_P)=h^q(S,\OO_S)=(1,2,1)$, and its canonical
section has the divisor \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.2}.
It is the unique minimum-order component for canonical evaluation;
the differences of the other orders are exactly \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.1}.
The zero-edge case, excluded from the nontrivial tree here,
is the smooth torus fibre already treated in \ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.5}.
\end{proposition}



\begin{proof}\leavevmode\par



 
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.,leftmargin=0pt,labelsep=.5em]
\item Every double curve has a nonroot endpoint.
At a Hopf endpoint, \cref{lem:II:hopf-curves} makes it
smooth elliptic and makes the distinct boundary curves
disjoint. At a quasibundle endpoint these properties
hold because the curves are distinct smooth fibre
supports. Hence there are no triple points, and the
curves on $P$ are also pairwise disjoint.

For each Hopf nonroot component use
\cref{lem:II:hopf-curve-restriction} for its coherent
dimensions and each given curve inclusion. For each
quasibundle use \cref{lem:II:identity-monodromy-elliptic}
with that same $q_v:T_v\to\PP^1$.
Equation \eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.3} and its restriction
square give dimensions $(1,1,0)$ and the nonzero
endpoint maps through its connected normal-root cover.
Compose at each edge with the given gluing map.
The rooted-tree clause of
\cref{lem:II:support-incidence-residues}, with root
this arbitrary $P$, now applies. It gives the
restriction isomorphisms \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.4}
through the normalization sequence
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.3}.

Flat semicontinuity gives $h^2(S,\OO_S)\ge1$,
and the compact-core bound of
\cref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.28} gives $p_g(P)\le1$.
Thus $p_g(P)=1$. Coherent Euler characteristic
is zero in this proper flat family. In the
normalization sequence every nonroot component
and every elliptic edge has coherent Euler
characteristic zero, so $\chi(\OO_P)=0$ and
$h^1(P,\OO_P)=2$. This proves both stated
coherent dimension vectors.

\item The same rooted-tree clause gives
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.5} by restriction to $P$
and extension by zero to the other components.
Its canonical evaluation comparison
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.HR.8} identifies $P$ as the
unique minimum-order component. Write its
order as $k_0$. The resulting holomorphic
two-form on $P$ has exact divisor
\begin{equation}
          K_P=\sum_{e=(P,w)}(k_w-k_0-1)J_e,\qquad
                          k_w>k_0.
 \hypertarget{tag-00W9}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.PT.6}
\end{equation}
Its coefficients are nonnegative integers,
and its section has no zero away from this
boundary. A rational exceptional curve
$E$ of square $-1$ would satisfy
$K_P\cdot E=-1$ by adjunction. Each curve
in the displayed effective divisor is
elliptic and different from $E$, so their
intersections with $E$ are nonnegative.
This contradiction proves minimality of $P$.

\item \par\medskip\noindent\textbf{The actual elliptic fibration on the root.}
Its nonzero canonical form gives $\kappa(P)\ge0$.
Every component has full multiplicity one, and the
given total space and central support are already
smooth and SNC. Thus the actual common-root map in
\ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.31} has degree one and its component over $P$ is
$P$ itself. That theorem makes $P$ a two-torus or
gives on it a fixed-modulus, identity-monodromy
elliptic quasi-bundle with only smooth multiples.
Its base has genus $p_g(P)=1$.


\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=1.3em,labelsep=.5em]
\item For a principal $F=\C/\Lambda_F$-torsor over an elliptic $B$, use \cref{lem:II:zero-chern-elliptic-torsor} with $F_1=F$ and $\Gamma=\Lambda_B$. The map in \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.7} is its integral Chern map, and for Chern class zero \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.8} is the resulting isomorphism over this same $B$, preserving the analytic torsor class. We apply this to the root fibration below and to the inverse torsor $T_0\to B$ after its Chern class is computed.

\item  We now identify every marked elliptic curve on $P$
with a fibre of one such elliptic fibration.
On a torus an elliptic curve is a translate of an
elliptic subtorus: lifting its map to universal
covers makes its derivative a periodic holomorphic
function, hence constant. Two different elliptic
directions give an isogeny from their product to
the two-torus, so their translates intersect.
The pairwise disjoint boundary curves therefore
have the same direction and are fibres of the
actual quotient by that elliptic subtorus.


\item  In the other alternative let $q:P\to B$ be the
fibration supplied by \ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.31}. If it has a multiple
fibre, any nonvertical marked elliptic curve would
map finitely to the elliptic $B$. Riemann--Hurwitz
makes that map unramified. But at a multiple fibre
the actual local function is $s^m$, $m>1$,
so the restriction to that curve has positive
ramification, a contradiction.
If there is no multiple fibre, $q$ is a principal
$F$-torsor. A nonvertical elliptic curve would give
a section after its finite base pullback. Pullback
on $H^2(B,\Lambda_F)$ multiplies its Chern vector
by the positive covering degree. The vector group
is torsion-free, so the original vector would be
zero. Apply \cref{lem:II:zero-chern-elliptic-torsor} with total space $E_1=P$, base $B$ and fixed curve $F_1=F$. Its map \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.8} identifies this root torsor with a two-torus over $B$, giving the torus case above. Otherwise all marked
curves are vertical. Since every reduced fibre
is one smooth elliptic curve, each is exactly
a marked fibre support. This proves the required
actual fibration $q_P$ in all cases.


\end{enumerate}

\item Apply \cref{lem:II:identity-monodromy-elliptic}
to the root map $q_P$ just constructed. Its normal-root
chart gives finite exact normal order at each marked
fibre. Duality carries that order to the adjacent
component. The nontorsion-axis calculation of
\cref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.58} excludes a first diagonal
algebraic-dimension-zero vertex along any path from
$P$. All such vertices are therefore absent.
A nonlinear Hopf component has its unique elliptic
curve and is terminal. Every other nonroot component
has the given genus-zero quasibundle, or the elliptic
Hopf reduction of \cref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.37}.
The boundary curves are fibre supports of these
maps. For an elliptic Hopf component this follows
from its vanishing rational second cohomology and
positivity of intersection, as in
\cref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.58}.

Apply the rooted domain of
\cref{lem:II:support-heights-period} to these
same maps, the distinguished $q_P:P\to B$,
the given full reduced SNC smoothing, and its
normal dualities. It excludes every unmarked
multiple fibre, identifies the connected normal
roots along the tree, and gives the common
Jacobian with its edge maps. Its integer
equation \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.9} gives precisely
the heights \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.1}; at the
root its canonical section has divisor
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.2}.

Its collar comparison \eqref{cdp:eq:C.HT.10}
uses this same $xy=t$ smoothing and its
normal products. At a nonlinear leaf its
map \eqref{cdp:eq:C.SN.6} includes the full
secondary integer and both primitive fibre
circles. Thus its integral class is the
class of every regular fibre of these
given quasibundles, including the root.
Equations \cref{cdp:eq:C.HT.11,cdp:eq:C.PT.10}
are the expansions of that one period
for the evaluation divided by $t^{k_0}$.
They give the stated common value $R$ at
nonlinear leaves and the strict inequalities
at quasibundle vertices. This proves the
height test in every actual occurrence.

\item \par\medskip\noindent\textbf{The exact inverse torsor and its integral obstruction.}
Perform the operations (C.PR.6) from the leaves
inward. After its children have been removed,
an elliptic nonroot vertex retains its actual
fixed-Jacobian map over $\PP^1$: each operation
replaced exactly the specified multiple-fibre
tube by the ordinary product tube and left
all other transitions unchanged. Its only
possible multiple fibre is now the parent
mark. It is therefore the actual one-mark
torsor of (C.PR.1)--(C.PR.5), hence is a
recorded diagonal Hopf pair or the product
ruled cap. The root-line classification retains
its entire torsor, even when the original
unpruned surface had Kodaira dimension one.
Nonlinear leaves use the same
inverse product map, with their full
secondary integer and primitive fibre
direction. The root always remains its
fixed-Jacobian quasi-bundle over the original
elliptic $B$. Each operation replaces exactly
one marked multiple-fibre tube by its
displayed ordinary product tube; a product
cap leaves that ordinary tube unchanged.
There are no unmarked multiples. After all
nonroot vertices have been removed, the final
root is therefore a principal $F$-torsor
$T_0\to B$, with its full analytic transition
class retained.


\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=1.3em,labelsep=.5em]
\item  The exact boundary homomorphism of every
removed compact piece is (C.PR.9): it kills
the one meridian $\delta$ and retains the
two generators $e,h$. The inverse product
filling has those identical maps. Applying
the actual Van Kampen pushouts successively,
as in \ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.60}, gives
\[
                         \pi_1(T_0)\simeq\pi_1(F_t)
                                             \simeq\Z^4.
 \tag{C.PT.11}\hypertarget{tag-00W1}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.PT.11}
\]
Only these smooth collar maps are used for
an arbitrary original degeneration; no
holomorphic contraction of its neighbourhood
is asserted.


\item  For a principal elliptic bundle over an
elliptic curve the homotopy sequence has
an injected fibre lattice, since
$\pi_2(B)=0$. The group is the central
extension
\[
 1\longrightarrow\Lambda_F
 \longrightarrow\pi_1(T_0)
 \longrightarrow\Lambda_B\longrightarrow1.
 \tag{C.PT.12}\hypertarget{tag-00W2}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.PT.12}
\]
The commutator of lifts of an oriented
base basis is its integral Chern vector.
This follows directly by trivializing over
the usual base parallelogram: its boundary
commutator is the clutching loop of the
fibre torus. Equation \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.11} makes that
commutator zero in the injected lattice.
Thus the Chern vector is zero. Apply \cref{lem:II:zero-chern-elliptic-torsor} with $(E_1,B,F_1)=(T_0,B,F)$ to this inverse torsor. Its local translation cochain and quotient map \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.8} preserve that torsor's analytic class and identify its total space with a complex two-torus over $B$. This proves
necessity of the last test. Independence
of disjoint pruning orders is the actual
chart comparison of \ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.60}.


\end{enumerate}

\item \par\medskip\noindent\textbf{Compact reconstruction of the complete prescribed tree.}
Assume all the tests pass and retain the
complete pruning record. Formula \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.8}
gives the actual initial torus
$T_0=\C^2/\Gamma$. Its elliptic fibre
lattice is a primitive rank-two subgroup
of $\Gamma$, because the quotient base
lattice is free. Choose $R$ as in the
height test and put
\[
 V_t(w)=w+t^R J\overline w,\qquad
              J=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{C.PT.13}\hypertarget{tag-00W3}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.PT.13}
\]
For any real basis of $\Gamma$ its image
has determinant $(1+|t|^{2R})^2$ times
the original nonzero determinant.
These holomorphic period sections
therefore give a proper smooth torus
family on the finite chart. At infinity
the frame divided by $t^R$ gives
$J\overline w+s^Rw$, $s=t^{-1}$.
It is again real-linearly invertible
at every point, including $s=0$.
The two charts consequently give an
actual compact smooth torus family
over $\PP^1$, with central member
exactly $T_0$.


\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=1.3em,labelsep=.5em]
\item  For an oriented primitive fibre basis
$\lambda,\mu=c\lambda$,
$\operatorname{Im}c>0$, its exact period
in this frame is
\[
 \det_{\C}(V_t\lambda,V_t\mu)
       =2i\operatorname{Im}(c)\|\lambda\|^2t^R.
 \tag{C.PT.14}\hypertarget{tag-00W4}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.PT.14}
\]
The coefficient is nonzero. Near each
recorded central elliptic fibre use
the actual rank-two period cover and
the primitive-basis change (C.PR.13).
This gives
$(p,w)\mapsto(p+\delta(t),\gamma(t)w)$
with $\delta(t)=t^R d(t)$, $d(0)\ne0$,
and the original marked Jacobian and
primitive fibre direction.


\item  Reverse the pruning record. At a
recorded Hopf step of weight $m$ use
the free weighted chart (C.PR.14),
including its full secondary integer.
Its child's affine pencil has the
exact displacement $\delta(t)/t^m$.
At a product-cap step use the ordinary
blowup (C.PR.16), with displacement
$\delta(t)/t$. Thus the remaining
order at every vertex is $R-h_v$.
The height test makes each recorded
elliptic child linear and every
recorded nonlinear terminal child
nonlinear, with its prescribed
resonance and contraction. The
recorded primitive basis changes
retain all linear gluing maps,
and the retained transition charts
restore all elliptic translations
and every analytic torsor. In particular an
original properly elliptic nonroot surface
is restored by reversing its successive
root-line and ordinary-tube changes. No
replacement by a surface with only the same
degrees or normal characters occurs.


\item  All local compactness comparisons
are precisely (C.PR.17)--(C.PR.18).
Exponential contraction dominates
the polynomial exceptional norm
distortion, and the old base
displacement is
$O(|\delta(t)|\,|\log|x||)$.
Its cluster set lies in the old
marked elliptic curve. These exact
bounds give disjoint Hausdorff
proper replacements at each stage;
ordinary caps are proper blowups.
There are finitely many stages.
Each is the identity on the
punctured family and outside its
chosen small central neighbourhood.
They therefore preserve the
compact family over the rest of
$\PP^1$, including infinity.


\item  Induction through the recorded
inverse charts restores precisely
the specified $P$, every nonroot
component and each prescribed
elliptic gluing map. Their normal
equations are the free coarse
$t=xW$ charts or the ordinary
$t=xy$ charts, so the full fibre
is reduced and the total space
is smooth. Every other fibre is
the unchanged smooth torus.
The root quasi-bundle and every supplied
genus-zero quasi-bundle have Euler number
zero by additivity over their smooth
elliptic fibre supports. Every remaining
Hopf component and every double elliptic
curve also has Euler number zero. Additivity proves
the stated zero Euler number
for $S$ and for all other supports.


\item  The rooted incidence matrices,
the integral Chern commutator,
the exact torsor period matrix
and the height equations are
checked in
\path{code/A_rooted_hopf_trees.py};
the primitive period and nested
order identities are also
certified in
\path{code/A_tree_periods.py}.



\end{enumerate}

\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Rooted elliptic supports]\hypertarget{tag-01E7}{}\label{cdp:st:C.2.UN.61}
\StatementRecord{cdp:st:C.2.UN.61}{proved}{01E7}{\cref{lem:II:identity-monodromy-elliptic,lem:II:support-incidence-residues,lem:II:support-heights-period,lem:II:elliptic-tree-pruning,lem:II:elliptic-star-boundary,lem:II:zero-chern-elliptic-torsor,lem:II:compact-elliptic-star-insertion,cdp:st:C.2.UN.31}}
Let $S$ be a compact connected reduced SNC surface whose incidence
graph is a nontrivial tree, with a distinguished smooth component
$P$. Every other component is a primary or secondary Hopf surface,
or has a fixed-Jacobian elliptic quasibundle map to $\PP^1$ with
connected fibres, identity integral monodromy and only smooth
multiple supports. The boundary curves of a quasibundle are fibre
supports of its given map. The elliptic gluing maps and analytic
torsors are included in the data.

Occurrence of $S$ as a full fibre of a degeneration of connected
complex two-tori from a smooth total space is equivalent to:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The two normal lines at every double curve are dual.
\item The root has a fixed-Jacobian elliptic quasibundle
$q_P:P\to B$ over a smooth elliptic curve, with identity integral
monodromy and only smooth multiple supports. Its boundary curves
are fibres and every multiple fibre is marked. Every nonroot
component is a nonlinear algebraic-dimension-zero Hopf leaf, or
an elliptic quasibundle over $\PP^1$ of the indicated type whose
multiple fibres are all marked.
\item Each edge normal has exact finite order $m_e$, equal to
its full elliptic multiplicity or nonlinear resonance.
For the heights \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.1}, with $V_0=\{P\}$, there is
an integer $R>0$ with $h_v=R$ at every nonlinear leaf and $h_v<R$
at every elliptic nonroot vertex. With no nonlinear leaves any
$R>\max_v h_v$ suffices.
\item The pruning maps of \cref{lem:II:elliptic-tree-pruning} give
a principal elliptic torsor $T_0\to B$ whose integral Chern vector
in $H^2(B,\Lambda_F)$ is zero. This is the torsor defined by the
complete inverse charts, primitive bases and secondary integers.
\end{enumerate}
The connected normal-root maps identify the fixed Jacobian $F$
along the tree. Disjoint pruning steps give the same marked
torsor up to the isomorphisms of \cref{lem:II:elliptic-tree-pruning}.

Every support satisfying these conditions has a realization over
$\PP^1$ with smooth compact total threefold, with the given $S$
as its only singular fibre and all other fibres smooth two-tori.
Every component, analytic torsor and elliptic gluing map is
preserved. All reduced fibre supports have Euler number zero.
In every occurrence the root is minimal and
$h^q(P,\OO_P)=h^q(S,\OO_S)=(1,2,1)$. It is the unique minimum-order
component for canonical evaluation, its canonical divisor is
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.2}, and all order differences are the heights
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.1}. The zero-edge case is the smooth torus
fibre of \cref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.5}.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Each double curve has a nonroot endpoint. On a Hopf component,
\cref{lem:II:hopf-curves} makes its curves smooth elliptic and
pairwise disjoint. On a quasibundle they are distinct smooth
fibre supports. Hence there are no triple points and the curves
on $P$ are also disjoint.

For every Hopf nonroot component apply
\cref{lem:II:hopf-curve-restriction} to its curve inclusions;
for every quasibundle apply
\cref{lem:II:identity-monodromy-elliptic} to its given map
$q_v:T_v\to\PP^1$. Its coherent formula and root-restriction
square give dimensions $(1,1,0)$ and nonzero endpoint maps through
the connected normal-root covers. Compose with the given gluing
map at each edge. The rooted clause of
\cref{lem:II:support-incidence-residues} applies with the unrestricted
root $P$. It identifies the normalization sequence
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.3} and restriction isomorphisms
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.4} with those of this $S$.

Semicontinuity gives $h^2(S,\OO_S)\ge1$, and
\cref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.28} gives $p_g(P)\le1$; hence $p_g(P)=1$.
Flatness gives $\chi(\OO_S)=0$. Every nonroot component and every
edge has coherent Euler characteristic zero, so the normalization
sequence gives $\chi(\OO_P)=0$ and $h^1(P,\OO_P)=2$.
The same rooted clause gives \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.5} by restriction
to $P$ and extension by zero on the other components.
Its canonical evaluation map \eqref{cdp:eq:C.HR.8} makes $P$
the unique minimum-order component. With minimum $k_0$, its
holomorphic two-form has divisor
\begin{equation}
 K_P=\sum_{e=(P,w)}(k_w-k_0-1)J_e,\qquad k_w>k_0.
\hypertarget{tag-00W9}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.PT.6}
\end{equation}
All coefficients are nonnegative. A rational exceptional curve
$E$ with $E^2=-1$ would have $K_P\cdot E=-1$ by adjunction,
whereas its intersections with these distinct elliptic curves
are nonnegative. Thus $P$ is minimal.

The nonzero canonical form gives $\kappa(P)\ge0$. The component
multiplicities are one and the total space is smooth, so the
common-root map of \cref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.31} has degree one over
$P$. Its component is $P$ itself. That theorem makes $P$ a
two-torus or gives it a fixed-modulus, identity-monodromy elliptic
quasibundle with base genus $p_g(P)=1$.

On a two-torus an elliptic curve is a translate of an elliptic
subtorus: the derivative of its lift is periodic and holomorphic,
hence constant. Two distinct elliptic directions give an isogeny
from their product onto the torus, so any translates intersect.
The disjoint boundary curves therefore have one direction and
are fibres of the quotient by that subtorus.
For the other elliptic map $q:P\to B$, a horizontal marked elliptic
curve maps finitely and unramifiedly to $B$ by Riemann--Hurwitz.
At a full multiple fibre the local base function is $s^m$, forcing
ramification on such a curve. Thus the presence of a multiple
fibre makes every marked curve vertical. With no multiple fibre,
$q$ is a principal $F$-torsor. A horizontal elliptic curve gives a
section after its finite base pullback. This pullback multiplies
the integral Chern vector by its positive degree in the torsion-free
group $H^2(B,\Lambda_F)$, so that vector is zero.
Apply \cref{lem:II:zero-chern-elliptic-torsor} to
$(E_1,B,F_1)=(P,B,F)$. Its translation cochain and map
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.8} identify this analytic torsor over $B$ with
a two-torus, to which the preceding quotient argument applies.
In all cases there is a map $q_P$ with every marked curve as a
fibre support.

The connected root chart of \cref{lem:II:identity-monodromy-elliptic},
now on this same $q_P$, gives finite normal order at each root mark.
The dual-normal isomorphism carries that order to its neighbour.
The infinite-order diagonal axes in \cref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.58} therefore
cannot occur at the first such vertex along a path from $P$.
Every nonlinear Hopf has one elliptic axis and is a leaf.
Every other nonroot component has its given genus-zero map or the
Hopf reduction of \cref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.37}; the latter's boundary
curves are fibres by $H^2(H,\Q)=0$ and positivity of a horizontal
intersection with a fibre.

Apply the rooted domain of \cref{lem:II:support-heights-period}
to these maps, $q_P$, and the same normal-product smoothing.
It identifies all connected normal roots and their fixed Jacobian,
marks every multiple fibre, and gives the edge equations
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.9}, hence heights \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.1} and the
root divisor \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.2}. Its collar map
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.HT.10} and full secondary basis
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.SN.6} identify every regular fibre class, including
the root's class, with the integral core class. Its expansions
\cref{cdp:eq:C.HT.11,cdp:eq:C.PT.10} are therefore expansions of
one period of the evaluation divided by $t^{k_0}$. They give the
common $R$ and every strict height inequality.

Prune using \cref{lem:II:elliptic-tree-pruning} on these same maps.
Each step changes one multiple-fibre tube by
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.PR.6}, or removes a product cap by the identity
product map. All other transitions stay fixed. The final root
is a principal torsor $T_0\to B$ with the resulting analytic atlas.
The boundary map \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PR.9}, carried through the smooth
collars of the given degeneration, gives
\begin{equation}
                    \pi_1(T_0)\simeq\pi_1(F_t)\simeq\Z^4.
\hypertarget{tag-00W1}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.PT.11}
\end{equation}
Apply the principal-bundle group clause of
\cref{lem:II:elliptic-star-boundary} to this $T_0\to B$.
In its exact sequence \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.12}, the fibre lattice
is injected and the base commutator is the integral Chern vector.
Equation \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.11} makes that vector zero.
The map \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PT.8} of
\cref{lem:II:zero-chern-elliptic-torsor}, with
$(E_1,B,F_1)=(T_0,B,F)$, then identifies the same analytic torsor
with its two-torus quotient. This proves the last necessary
condition, and the pruning lemma gives the stated independence.

Conversely use this zero-Chern inverse torsor, the complete inverse
pruning maps and the heights in
\cref{lem:II:compact-elliptic-star-insertion}. Its root is exactly
$T_0$, its initial period has order $R$, and each next displacement
has order $R-h_v$ by \eqref{cdp:eq:C.PR.15} or
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.PR.16}. Its reverse maps recover $P$ and all other
components with their full torsors and marked gluing maps.
Its proper compact realization has this reduced $S$ as its only
singular fibre and smooth two-tori elsewhere. Its Euler conclusion
applies to the same components and double curves, proving all
remaining assertions.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Unicyclic supports with elliptic quasi-bundle torsors]\hypertarget{tag-01E8}{}\label{cdp:st:C.2.UN.62}
\StatementRecord{cdp:st:C.2.UN.62}{proved}{01E8}{\SeriesRef{cdp:st:C.2.UN.60}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.QT.2}, \SeriesRef{cdp:st:C.2.UN.54}, \SeriesRef{cdp:st:C.2.UN.50}, \SeriesRef{cdp:st:C.2.UN.44}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.QT.3}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.QT.7}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.QT.6}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.QT.8}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.QT.5}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.QT.9}, \SeriesRef{cdp:st:C.2.UN.57}, \SeriesRef{cdp:eq:C.QT.11}}

Let $S$ be a specified compact connected SNC surface with smooth
embedded components. Each component is either a nonlinear primary
or secondary Hopf surface of algebraic dimension zero, or is
equipped with an actual map
\[
                         q_v:T_v\longrightarrow\PP^1
\tag{C.QT.1}\hypertarget{tag-00WD}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.QT.1}
\]
with connected fibres, every fibre a multiple of a smooth elliptic
curve, fixed elliptic Jacobian, and identity monodromy on the
integral first cohomology of the regular fibre. Every boundary
curve on $T_v$ is a fibre support of this specified map. The
elliptic gluing maps, the surfaces and their complete analytic
torsors are part of the data.

The following geometric test is necessary and sufficient for
$S$ to occur as a full reduced fibre of a smooth-total
degeneration of connected complex two-tori.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The actual boundary normal lines are dual, and the incidence
graph has exactly one independent cycle. Nonlinear Hopf vertices
are leaves.
\item Every multiple fibre of every map \eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.1} is marked by
a boundary curve. Let $m_e$ be the exact order of its normal
line, also the normal order at the other endpoint. At a
nonlinear endpoint this is its resonance.
\item Set $h_v=0$ on the cycle and set $h_v$ equal to the sum
of the $m_e$ along its path from the cycle. There is an integer
$R>0$ for which every nonlinear leaf has height $R$ and every
elliptic quasi-bundle vertex has height strictly smaller than
$R$. With no nonlinear leaves one may choose any
$R>\max_v h_v$.
\item Apply the exact inverse-logarithmic and product-cap
pruning maps of \ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.60}, retaining their full integer
framings and all torsor identifications. The resulting
marked diagonal Hopf or degree-zero ruled core cycle has
integral complement-lattice product $M=I$.
\end{enumerate}
All pruning operations in this test exist under its preceding
requirements. Their marked result is independent of the order
of disjoint branch operations. Every support passing the test
has a realization over $\PP^1$ with smooth compact total space,
retaining every original component, analytic torsor and
specified elliptic gluing map. The only other singular support
is the complex conjugate of its pruned core. Every reduced
fibre support has Euler number zero.

In particular the statement includes elliptic quasi-bundles
of Kodaira dimension one and coherent Euler characteristic
zero, together with the genus-zero quasi-bundle components
of Kodaira dimension zero and the Hopf and ruled components
in the same explicitly specified class.
\end{proposition}



\begin{proof}\leavevmode\par



 
\begin{enumerate}[label=\arabic*.,leftmargin=0pt,labelsep=.5em]
\item Each given quasibundle
$q_v:T_v\to\PP^1$ is relatively minimal,
because its vertical primes are elliptic.
Apply \cref{lem:II:identity-monodromy-elliptic}
to this same map and each marked full fibre.
Its quotient \eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.2} is the
normalized root of that fibre, and its
primitive character gives the exact normal
order. Formula \eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.3} gives
the coherent dimensions and the commuting
restriction and root-pullback square.
For a nonlinear component use
\cref{lem:II:hopf-curve-restriction}; for
its secondary normal character use
\cref{def:II:elliptic-star-data}.
All boundary curves on each component are
disjoint, so the SNC support has no
triple points.

For an actual full reduced occurrence,
the first clause of
\cref{lem:II:support-incidence-residues}
applies to these components and exactly
these restriction and gluing maps. Its
normalization sequence is
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.4}. It gives the
unicyclic graph, product-one coherent
holonomy, dimensions \eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.5},
and the minimum canonical order precisely
on the cycle.

\item Apply the first domain of
\cref{lem:II:support-heights-period} with
the given maps \eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.1},
the same nonlinear leaves and all the
normal-product identifications from the
smooth-total occurrence. The component
divisor is \eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.7}; its
vertical-form expression and order are
\cref{cdp:eq:C.HT.5,cdp:eq:C.QT.6} in
\cref{lem:II:identity-monodromy-elliptic}.
That lemma consequently excludes
unmarked multiples, gives the exact
edge and degree equations
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.8}, and identifies
the path heights and the base forms
$c\,dz/z$ and $c\,dz$ on the same
cycle and tree vertices. Its root-square
comparison also proves that the lifted
elliptic cycle product has identity
linear part, with its translation
unchanged.

The common integral class is obtained
by the normal-root collars of this
smoothing and the full secondary
boundary maps of its nonlinear leaves.
Its regular and nonlinear expansions
are \cref{cdp:eq:C.QT.9,cdp:eq:C.QT.10}
for the canonical evaluation divided
by its cycle minimum. A nonlinear leaf
fixes the one finite order $R$;
every other nonlinear leaf has that
height and every quasibundle vertex
has smaller height. With no nonlinear
leaf, any integer above all the
finitely many heights meets the
stated height requirement. This
proves necessity of the first three
conditions for the full given
quasibundle class.

\item \par\medskip\noindent\textbf{Pruning with the full torsors.}
The pruning proof of \ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.60} applies to the
maps \eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.1} themselves. We specify the
comparisons that retain the present
broader surface class. Delete a terminal
nonlinear Hopf by the inverse chart
(C.PR.6), with its full primitive period
basis and integer $n$. After the children
of an elliptic vertex have been removed,
its actual modified map still has fixed
Jacobian and identity monodromy over
$\PP^1$; each inverse operation replaced
one multiple fibre by the displayed
ordinary product tube and changed no
other transition. Its only possible
multiple fibre is now its parent mark.


\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=1.3em,labelsep=.5em]
\item  It is therefore the actual $F$-torsor
on $\PP^1[(\infty,m)]$ classified by
(C.PR.1)--(C.PR.5). The exact logarithm
sequence and $H^1(\OO)=H^2(\OO)=0$
identify the entire torsor with its
two root-line classes. A nonzero
vector gives the literal weighted
Hopf quotient, including $n$ and
the primitive fibre direction;
a zero vector forces $m=1$ and
the product ruled cap. This conclusion
concerns the actual modified surface,
even when its original unmodified
surface had Kodaira dimension one.
Remove that pair by its corresponding
map and retain the entire inverse
record.


\item  At the end the two-mark root-stack
cover (C.PR.7) and its actual line
pushout identify each core vertex
with a marked diagonal Hopf surface
or the torsion ruled bundle (C.PR.8).
These are exact maps on the original
transition atlases. Disjoint branch
operations commute on those atlases,
so their marked result has the
independence stated in \ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.60}.


\item  For an actual degeneration, every
terminal complement and its inverse
product cap have the identical
boundary homomorphism (C.PR.9),
retaining both elliptic generators
and killing exactly the specified
primitive meridian. The van Kampen
pushouts are identical on the
unchanged exterior. Their iteration
identifies the core plumbing group
with the original $\Z^4$. The
injected-lattice semidirect product
for that core consequently has
$M=I$. This proves necessity of
the last test by actual group maps.


\end{enumerate}

\item \par\medskip\noindent\textbf{Compact restoration of every prescribed component.}
Conversely suppose the test passes.
Use the compact marked core of \ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.57}
with the power $V_{t^R}$ and the
unchanged logarithmic coefficient
of (C.PR.11). Its necks remain
$xy=t$ and its opposite filling
is the conjugate pruned core.
The compact elliptic subgroup of
its common open group is the
actual regular-fibre group, and
(C.PR.12) makes its transverse
period determinant a nonzero
constant times $t^R$.


\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=1.3em,labelsep=.5em]
\item  Reverse the entire pruning record.
At a vertex of height $h$, the
local quotient (C.PR.13) has
displacement of order $R-h$.
The recorded primitive basis is
implemented by the displayed
unimodular linear period map
following (C.PR.13). At a Hopf
step, the weight-$(m,1)$ insertion
with $\OO(nE)$ has exactly the
free finite chart (C.PR.14).
The new child's coordinate
$U=Z/W^m$ gives the actual
displacement $\delta(t)/t^m$,
as in (C.PR.15). At a product
cap the ordinary blowup has
the exact displacement
$\delta(t)/t$, as in (C.PR.16).
The height test makes all these
maps holomorphic and gives
precisely the prescribed diagonal
or nonlinear central type.


\item  All operations use the entire
recorded inverse transitions.
In particular an original
properly elliptic vertex is
restored by reversing the
successive changes of its
root lines and ordinary tubes;
its complete analytic torsor,
all multiple fibres and all
marked points reappear, rather
than only its degree or normal
characters. The strict-parent
map is exactly (C.PR.6) in the
opposite direction. The same
argument applies to every
other original quasi-bundle.
Fibre translations and the
recorded linear maps retain
each specified elliptic gluing.


\item  The norm and affine-base bounds
(C.PR.17)--(C.PR.18) prove the
actual local properness and
the old-cluster comparison for
each replacement. Their constants
depend on the local displacement
order and contraction, not on the
Kodaira dimension of the surface
being restored. The finitely many
disjoint replacements therefore
give the same Hausdorff compact
gluing as \ref{cdp:st:C.2.UN.60}. The weighted
free coordinates have $t=xW$;
ordinary cap charts have $t=xy$.
Every final component consequently
has full multiplicity one.


\item  Each component \eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.1} has Euler
number zero by additivity over
its elliptic fibre supports;
each nonlinear Hopf also has
Euler number zero. Every double
curve is elliptic and there are
no triple points. Both special
supports thus have Euler zero,
as do the general tori. This
proves the complete criterion
and the compact assertion.


\end{enumerate}

\item \par\medskip\noindent\textbf{An explicit properly elliptic component.}
Fix $F=\C^*/\beta^{\Z}$, $0<|\beta|<1$.
Start with the two-component
ruled core $F\times\PP^1$
glued along its two marked
sections by the identity.
Its lattice product is the
identity. On one component
choose four distinct ordinary
fibre points away from those
sections. Perform four recorded
weight-three, secondary-order-one
insertions, with the common
period order $R=3$.
They add four nonlinear primary
Hopf leaves $H_3(\beta)$.


\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*),leftmargin=1.3em,labelsep=.5em]
\item  The modified central component
has an explicit independent
description. Put
\[
 \mathcal B=\PP^1[(p_1,3),\ldots,(p_4,3)],\qquad
 L=\OO_{\mathcal B}(D_1+\cdots+D_4),
 \qquad 3D_i=p_i.
\tag{C.QT.11}\hypertarget{tag-00WF}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.QT.11}
\]
It is the smooth coarse surface
of $L^\times/\beta^{\Z}$.
Each inertia acts by a primitive
fibre translation, so its coarse
surface is smooth and its four
fibres are exactly triple smooth
elliptic curves. In a root chart
$p=s^3$ its line coordinate is
$y=sW$, where $W$ is the old
product coordinate. The inverse
chart (C.PR.6) with $m=3,n=1$
has precisely $W=y/s$.
Thus this given line pushout
is the component produced by
the four insertions, including
its full torsor.
Explicitly the positive divisor
line has frames $e_{\rm in}=s^{-1}e_{\rm out}$.
The equality of the actual vector
$W e_{\rm out}=y e_{\rm in}$
is precisely $y=sW$; its canonical
section has local coefficient $s$.
This fixes the sign of each $D_i$
in \eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.11}.


\item  For any map of the class
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.1}, the actual invariant
fibre differential and the
root chart give the plurigenus
formula
\[
 h^0(T_v,\omega_{T_v}^{\otimes a})
 =\max\left\{0,\ 1-2a+
       \sum_i\left\lfloor
                    a(1-1/m_i)\right\rfloor\right\}.
\tag{C.QT.12}\hypertarget{tag-00WG}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.QT.12}
\]

is a base meromorphic
$a$-differential times the
$a$th invariant fibre factor;
holomorphy at a root chart
permits precisely the displayed
pole order. Descent and its
inverse are those actual
invariant-coordinate maps.

\[
 h^0(T,\omega_T^{\otimes a})
    =\max\{0,1-2a+4\lfloor2a/3\rfloor\},
 \qquad \omega_T^{\otimes3}\simeq q^*\OO_{\PP^1}(2).
\tag{C.QT.13}\hypertarget{tag-00WH}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.QT.13}

$q(T)=1$, $\chi(\OO_T)=0$
and $h^0(T,\omega_T^{\otimes3b})=2b+1$.
Thus this is an actual properly
elliptic component. The complete
compact reduced fibre consists
of it, the unchanged ruled core
component, and the four Hopf
leaves, with every gluing given
by the preceding maps.

matrix, the root-coordinate pole
bounds and these exact plurigenera
are checked in
\path{code/D_quasibundle_trees.py}
and its saved output.



\end{enumerate}

\end{enumerate}
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Plurigenera and a four-fibre elliptic component]\hypertarget{tag-P376}{}\label{prop:II:elliptic-quasibundle-plurigenera}
\StatementRecord{prop:II:elliptic-quasibundle-plurigenera}{proved}{P376}{\cref{lem:II:identity-monodromy-elliptic,lem:II:compact-elliptic-star-insertion,cdp:st:C.2.UN.62}}
For a genus-zero identity-monodromy quasibundle
$q:T\to\PP^1$ with full multiple fibres $m_iJ_i$, its plurigenera are
\begin{equation}
 h^0(T,\omega_T^{\otimes a})
 =\max\left\{0,1-2a+\sum_i
              \left\lfloor a(1-1/m_i)\right\rfloor\right\},
                                      \qquad a\ge1.
\hypertarget{tag-00WG}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.QT.12}
\end{equation}
There is a compact smooth-total two-torus degeneration whose
reduced singular fibre has a quasibundle component with four
triple fibres and Kodaira dimension one, one elliptic ruled
component, and four nonlinear primary Hopf leaves of resonance
three. All its elliptic gluing maps are the maps below.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
The invariant vertical differential and root charts of
\cref{lem:II:identity-monodromy-elliptic}, applied to this $q$,
identify a pluricanonical section with a meromorphic base
$a$-differential times the $a$th invariant fibre factor.
At $t=s^{m_i}$ its order is
$m_i\operatorname{ord}_{t=0}\theta+a(m_i-1)$.
Holomorphy therefore permits a base pole of order at most
$\lfloor a(1-1/m_i)\rfloor$. Descent in this invariant chart
and pullback by the same root map are inverse to one another.
The resulting line on $\PP^1$ has degree
$-2a+\sum_i\lfloor a(1-1/m_i)\rfloor$, proving
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.QT.12}.

Fix $F=\C^*/\beta^{\Z}$ with $0<|\beta|<1$. Take two copies of
$F\times\PP^1$ and glue their fibres at zero and infinity by the
identity on $F$. This marked ruled cycle has $M=I$.
On one component choose four distinct ordinary base points away
from the two cycle marks. Use four weight-three insertions with
secondary integer one and period order $R=3$ in
\cref{lem:II:compact-elliptic-star-insertion}. They add the
nonlinear primary leaves $H_3(\beta)$.

The modified quasibundle component is explicitly the smooth coarse
surface of $L^\times/\beta^{\Z}$, where
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal B=\PP^1[(p_1,3),\ldots,(p_4,3)],\qquad
 L=\OO_{\mathcal B}(D_1+\cdots+D_4),\qquad 3D_i=p_i.
\hypertarget{tag-00WF}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.QT.11}
\end{equation}
Every inertia acts by a primitive fibre translation, giving a
smooth surface and exactly four triple fibres. In a root chart
$p=s^3$, its line coordinate is $y=sW$, with $W$ the product
coordinate before insertion. The inverse map
\eqref{cdp:eq:C.PR.6}, with $m=3,n=1$, is $W=y/s$.
For the positive divisor line the frames are
$e_{\rm in}=s^{-1}e_{\rm out}$, and the equality
$W e_{\rm out}=y e_{\rm in}$ gives exactly $y=sW$.
Its canonical section has coefficient $s$ in the inner frame.
These frame and inverse-root maps identify the complete line
torsor with the component in the compact construction.

The formula already proved gives
\begin{equation}
 h^0(T,\omega_T^{\otimes a})
       =\max\{0,1-2a+4\lfloor2a/3\rfloor\},\qquad
              \omega_T^{\otimes3}\simeq q^*\OO_{\PP^1}(2).
\hypertarget{tag-00WH}{}\label{cdp:eq:C.QT.13}
\end{equation}
Thus $p_g(T)=0$, $q(T)=1$, $\chi(\OO_T)=0$ and
$h^0(T,\omega_T^{\otimes3b})=2b+1$. The last equality gives
Kodaira dimension one. The other ruled component is unchanged;
the four Hopf leaves and every gluing are those of the displayed
inverse root charts. This is the asserted full compact fibre.
\end{proof}
